final_answer:
PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL - ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT
CREDENTIAL GAP ANALYSIS MEMO
To: Craig Halloran, Whitmore & Callahan LLP. Re: Prismex Analytics, Inc. / Dr. Ananya Mehrotra; PERM Case A-18247-63910 (ETA 9089 filed 3/15/2025, certified 5/22/2025); Senior Machine Learning Engineer. Source: HR package transmitted June 4, 2025 (nine matter documents).

1. BOTTOM LINE
(a) Education and the 5-year experience minimum are met on the documents. (b) The certification requirement ("AWS Certified Machine Learning - Specialty or equivalent") is NOT met: she holds no such certification, her only AWS credential is a foundational Cloud Practitioner that expired 1/18/2025, before the 3/15/2025 filing. Yet ETA 9089 K.3 and K.4 say "Yes." This is the critical defect. (c) Several skill requirements are met only thinly (R; Spark and SageMaker only since 2021; supervision of 2 vs. 3-5). (d) The package confuses the PERM (permanent residence) with the H-1B; the PERM does not support an I-129 and the H-1B has its own requirements. (e) Further record inconsistencies (FEIN, F-1/STEM OPT status, wage level) must be resolved before filing anything. Do not file the I-140 or I-129 on the current package until items 2.1, 4 and 5 are resolved.

2. REQUIREMENT-BY-REQUIREMENT COMPARISON (PERM J.B vs. credentials)
2.1 Certification (J.B.5; Addendum): "AWS Certified Machine Learning - Specialty certification or equivalent required." GAP - CRITICAL.
- Certifications compilation: Cloud Practitioner (foundational, issued 1/18/2022, expired 1/18/2025, not renewed; compilation itself says it does not demonstrate ML specialization). TensorFlow Developer Certificate (Google, 3/10/2023, active; framework-specific, not AWS). Counsel's own inquiry recorded that she holds no AWS specialty certification.
- "Or equivalent" is undefined in the 9089. Under the plain-language approach to labor certification terms (Matter of Silver Dragon Chinese Restaurant, 19 I&N Dec. 401 (Comm'r 1986), cited from memory), USCIS reads the terms as written and will not infer equivalence the form does not define. A foundational, expired credential is not plausibly equivalent to a specialty-level ML credential; the TensorFlow certificate is the only arguable candidate and the argument is weak (different vendor, framework-level, no cloud ML deployment/ops coverage). Her SageMaker work experience could be argued as "equivalent" in substance, but the form does not say experience may substitute, and J.B.4 states no alternate combination is accepted.
- Timing: the beneficiary must have met all stated requirements as of the priority date (here the 3/15/2025 filing date). Matter of Wing's Tea House, 16 I&N Dec. 158 (Acting Reg'l Comm'r 1977) (verified via search summary; Katigbak, 14 I&N Dec. 45, to the same effect, not independently verified). Obtaining the AWS ML Specialty exam now would not cure it.
- Consequence: K.3/K.4 "Yes" answers appear inaccurate on this record. Section L is under penalty of perjury (18 U.S.C. 1546 cited on the form); misstatement risks denial of the I-140, and DOL can invalidate a certification for fraud or willful misrepresentation (20 CFR 656.30(d), cited from memory). Also, the requirement was presumably used in recruitment; if U.S. applicants were rejected on a requirement the alien herself did not meet, that is a separate bona fide recruitment/656.17(i) exposure (the rule that the stated requirements be the employer's actual minimums, applied equally to U.S. workers). Recruitment advertisements and the recruitment report were not supplied; verify what they said. Note the 9089 reports that 2 of 3 U.S. applicants lacked education and 1 lacked experience; none is reported as rejected for lack of certification.

2.2 Education (J.B.1: Master's in CS, ML or closely related): MET. NC State M.S. Computer Science conferred 5/12/2018 (official transcript; GPA 3.74; thesis on transformer models for clinical text; coursework in Deep Learning, NLP, ML, R). The IAE evaluation (2/15/2025) covers only the B.Tech (ECE, four-year, equivalent to a U.S. bachelor's) and is not needed for the master's requirement; it is useful corroboration if EB-2 advanced-degree status (a U.S. master's) is later claimed. The ECE bachelor's field does not matter because the requirement is a master's.

2.3 Experience (J.B.3: 5 years progressive POST-master's experience in ML engineering or closely related occupation): MET, with caveats.
- Only DataBridge counts. Degree conferred 5/12/2018; DataBridge started 6/4/2018 (Data Scientist I to 1/3/2021; Data Scientist II from 1/4/2021; supervisor letter dated 4/10/2025; same facts in 9089 J.C and resume). By the 3/15/2025 priority date she had about 6 years 9 months, passing 5 years on 6/4/2023. The 9089 says "approximately 7 years" (K.2); that is overstated and should be corrected in I-140 narrative. Promotion supports "progressive."
- Evalpoint (7/1/2013-7/15/2016, software engineer) and NC State RA (8/15/2016-5/15/2018, 20 hrs/week) are PRE-master's (RA ended 3 days after conferral) and cannot count toward "post-master's" experience. The Evalpoint letter also undercuts the 9089's "related occupation" label: ML exposure was "ancillary," "ad hoc," "basic" scikit-learn. Conclusion: the missing NC State RA experience letter that HR flagged is NOT material to any stated requirement; the transcript (appointment, supervisor, NSF grant) suffices as background. Do not chase Professor Tsai; at most ask the department for a short confirmation if the RA is to be described in the I-140 or H-1B narrative.
- Caveat: the letter is from a data-science employer and the titles are "Data Scientist," while the requirement says "machine learning engineering or closely related." The same SOC (15-2051) and duty overlap make "closely related" supportable, but the DataBridge letter should say expressly that the work was ML engineering and production deployment.
- Letter sufficiency (8 CFR 204.5(g)(1), cited from memory: letters from employers giving name, address, title and specific duties): DataBridge letter is on letterhead, from the supervisor, with duties - adequate, but the copy in the package shows a blank signature line and does not map skills to periods or quantify (e.g., years using Spark, SageMaker, R). Both letters post-date the 3/15/2025 filing (4/10/2025 and 3/28/2025), so the attestation in the 9089 preceded written verification; confirm signed originals exist.

2.4 Special skills J.B.5 (a)-(e), measured against the DataBridge letter and resume:
(a) Production-grade deep learning in TensorFlow or PyTorch: MET (TensorFlow from 2018; both from 2021; production inference).
(b) Apache Spark: MET but only from DS II (1/4/2021), about 4 years 2 months at priority date; no per-skill duration is stated, so risk is low-moderate.
(c) NLP pipelines: MET (from 2018).
(d) Cloud ML deployment on AWS SageMaker or Vertex AI: MET only from 2021 (DS I used EC2). Same analysis as (b).
(e) Proficiency in Python and R: PARTIAL. Python strong. R is "some use of R for statistical reporting" (letter) and "intermediate"/"some use" (resume); the 9089 repeats this. A graduate R course (ST 558 A-) exists. The requirement says "proficiency in ... R," so USCIS could find "some use" inadequate. Recommend a supplemental DataBridge letter describing R projects, duration and scope.
(f) Supervision of 3-5 ML engineers and 10% travel: these are job duties, not beneficiary qualification requirements; she led 2 junior data scientists. Not a disqualifier unless USCIS treats the sentence in J.B.5 as a supervisory-experience requirement; the text says "Will supervise," future tense, and so should be treated as a duty. Flag, and have the employer confirm its drafting intent. Travel: no inconsistency.

3. PERM ACCURACY AND CONSISTENCY ISSUES
3.1 FEIN mismatch: ETA 9089 C.7 shows 84-3291756; the PWD shows 84-3291047. Verify against IRS records; correct whichever is wrong (affects PWD-to-PERM linkage and I-140/I-129 identity).
3.2 Prevailing wage: PWD is Level III, $131,747, based on a master's plus 5 years; the 9089 adds supervision of 3-5 staff and specialized-skills/certification requirements. Under DOL's wage-level guidance, extra experience, education, special skills and supervisory duties can raise the level to IV; the PWD narrative also oddly describes Level III as the mean of Levels III and IV, which does not match standard OES methodology. Whether the PWD request disclosed the supervisory duties and special skills is not shown. If the level is understated, the $142,000 offered wage might fall below the correct wage; the PWD expiry (11/7/2025) was satisfied because recruitment began 12/1/2024 (rule at 20 CFR 656.40(c), from memory). Recommend a check against the wage chart for the correct level before the H-1B LCA is filed. I could not retrieve the DOL guidance in this session; treat as flagged, not concluded.
3.4 Signature blocks on the supplied 9089 copy are blank, and the certifications compilation is unsigned/undated. Confirm signed originals before filing an I-140.

4. IMMIGRATION STATUS INCONSISTENCY
The 9089 lists current status F-1 (STEM OPT). She earned her master's in May 2018 and worked at DataBridge from 6/4/2018 to date. A post-completion OPT period plus the 24-month STEM extension (8 CFR 214.2(f)(10)(ii)(C), from memory) would have ended about mid-2021 at the latest. F-1 STEM OPT status in 2025 on these facts is not explained. Need her full immigration history (I-20s, EADs, I-94, any prior H-1B, change of status) to rule out unauthorized employment or a data error in the 9089. This also determines whether the H-1B is a change of status or consular process, and cap eligibility.

5. H-1B VS. PERM: WRONG VEHICLE
HR states the certified PERM means "we're good to move forward with the I-129." A certified PERM supports an I-140 (immigrant) petition, not an H-1B. The H-1B requires a certified LCA (ETA 9035) filed before the I-129, a specialty occupation (a bachelor's or higher in a specific specialty, 8 CFR 214.2(h)(4)(iii)(A)), the beneficiary's qualification, and, for cap-subject employers, a selected registration and a filing within the selected window. The package contains no LCA, no registration selection notice, no offer letter in the file (HR says signed), and no petition-specific job-duty documentation. The credentials that matter for H-1B are the CS master's (meets specialty occupation) and the position; the AWS certification gap is not itself an H-1B disqualifier, but statements inconsistent with the 9089 will be visible to USCIS, so the H-1B filing must not repeat the unsupported "meets all requirements" assertion. Nothing shows cap selection or an exemption. The offered $142,000 is only compared to an OES Level III wage; the LCA wage level should be assessed separately.

6. REMEDIAL RECOMMENDATIONS (priority order)
1. Immediately determine whether the AWS ML Specialty requirement was an actual minimum (check recruitment ads, recruitment report, job order, internal files). Do not file the I-140 on the current 9089 K.3/K.4 answers.
2. Choices on the certification gap: (a) the employer and counsel evaluate whether the requirement can be supported as satisfied by an "equivalent" through a detailed employer explanation and expert evidence (weak; risk of USCIS reading it narrowly); (b) withdraw/not use this certification and file a new PERM with corrected requirements (for example, certification "preferred," or alternate qualifying equivalents stated expressly) after new prevailing wage and recruitment, accepting lost time and a new priority date; (c) proceed only if the employer can truthfully explain the requirement was not a mandatory minimum - not supported by the text. Meanwhile, since the H-1B does not depend on the PERM, proceed with the H-1B on its own record (LCA, registration, specialty occupation) and consider whether to pursue the AWS ML Specialty exam for future use. Obtaining it now does not cure the priority-date deficiency.
3. Obtain a supplemental DataBridge letter (signed, with dates): ML engineering characterization; years using Spark, SageMaker, TensorFlow, PyTorch; R usage specifics; scope of leadership.
4. Resolve the FEIN discrepancy and immigration-status history before any filing.
5. Re-examine the wage level; consider a new PWD request if the correct level is higher; confirm the offered wage meets it.
6. Correct "approximately 7 years" to the exact period in any narrative; fix NOF description; obtain signed originals.
7. NC State RA letter: low priority; no further effort needed for PERM requirements.
8. Advise the client in writing of the above, including that the 9089 attestations were signed under penalty of perjury, and consider whether counsel's own preparer declaration (Section M) triggers professional-responsibility steps to correct a possible misstatement.

7. LIMITS
CFR text retrieval was blocked; cites marked from memory (and Silver Dragon, Katigbak) need cite-checking. Wing's Tea House confirmed by search summary only. No wage-level conclusion made.
